question: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), \(AC=3\) cm, \(BC=4\) cm, and \(AB=5\) cm. What is the distance from point \(C\) to line \(AB\), in cm? (Write your answer as a decimal.)
solution: Let the distance from point \(C\) to \(AB\) be \(h\). Equating the areas gives \(1/2\times3\times4=1/2\times5\times h\), so \(h=12/5=2.4\).

edges.reason: Point-to-point shortest-distance language is a helpful model, but perpendicular-shortest distance is a separate fact and not derived merely from the two-point line axiom.
The distance in question is the length of the perpendicular from the point, so perpendicularity identifies which segment is measured.
The similarity criteria parallel SSS, SAS and ASA, and similarity proofs use the same proof structure. Congruence experience is a strong preparatory analogy.
Similarity tests assert the similarity relation defined for polygons.
Subsidiary triangle similarity proves height/median ratios; direct property use is a different route.
